observations.finding: All 37 exact metric/dimension queries returned identical datapoint sets in two sweeps begun 6 and 12 minutes after the controlled end. Datapoints are preserved with native timestamp offsets; all controlled windows use UTC. No absent datapoint is represented as zero.

Every queried metric was absent in both complete idle-before-data minutes (10:18 and 10:19 UTC), both idle-after-client-closure minutes (10:26 and 10:27), and both idle-after-consumer-deregistration minutes (10:29 and 10:30). Specifically PutRecord.Success, PutRecords.Success and GetRecords.Success were absent, not zero. Their only points corresponded to actual successful operations.

Known put minute 10:20: stream IncomingBytes Count=2 Sum=18 Min=4 Max=14 Bytes; shard IncomingBytes Count=3 Sum=18 Min=4 Max=8 Bytes. Thus bytes include one partition-key byte per record, stream bytes aggregate the batch, and shard bytes sample its individual successful records. IncomingRecords is Count=2 Sum=3 Min=1 Max=2 at BOTH stream and shard dimensions.

Three successful standard reads returned respectively one record, two records at the tip, and no records. Their wire MillisBehindLatest were 60000,0,0. Both stream GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds and shard IteratorAgeMilliseconds had Count=3 Sum=60000 Min=0 Max=60000 Milliseconds. The last record of the caught-up data read was already 69458.141ms old at request start, so unconditional wall-clock arrival age is contradicted; the empty read also contributed a zero age sample.

Standard-read bytes/records have Count=3, including an observed zero sample for the empty successful read, unlike idle missingness. Bytes Sum=18 Min=0 Max=14; records Sum=3 Min=0 Max=2. Native GetRecords.Latency has 3 samples, Sum=23 Min=7 Max=8 Milliseconds; these are service observations, not client round-trip durations.

The one successful EFO subscription produced consumer-dimension SubscribeToShard.Success Count=1 Sum=1 Min=1 Max=1 and SubscribeToShard.RateExceeded Count=1 Sum=0 Min=0 Max=0, both Count units, in 10:22. Successful admission thus includes a measured zero rate-exceeded sample.

The complete active-empty EFO minute 10:24 contained 12 client-received empty events, and consumer Event.Bytes/Event.Records and shard OutgoingBytes/OutgoingRecords each had Count=12 Sum=0 Min=0 Max=0 (Bytes/Count units). Consumer Event.Success had Count=12 Sum=12 Min=1 Max=1 Count. These are active empty-delivery zeros, not idle traffic zeros.

All 38 received EFO events carried wire MillisBehindLatest=0. The replay data event was received 118030.216ms after its last record arrival, yet remained caught up (zero). Native consumer Event.MillisBehindLatest was zero in every sampled minute, with Count=12 in each complete subscription minute. The two live data events arrived 73.130ms and 109.886ms after record arrival; these timing anchors are not a latency distribution and must not replace backlog metric values.

EFO metrics appeared at exactly StreamName+ConsumerName; enhanced outgoing metrics appeared at StreamName+ShardId and included both standard reads and EFO deliveries in their respective minutes. EFO stream-only and StreamName+ConsumerName+ShardId queries returned no points. Stream-only OutgoingBytes/OutgoingRecords also had no points. Neither SubscribeToShard.Latency nor SubscribeToShardEvent.Latency was observed at consumer dimensions.

Near client closure (10:25) native Event.Success and outgoing metric Count=3 whereas only 2 client events were received that minute. The fixture does not identify when the extra service-side observation occurred or guarantee immediate cessation at client close. Subsequent complete 10:26 and 10:27 minutes were absent.
Owned consumer and stream were deleted and each returned ResourceNotFoundException. Cleanup preceded the lagged reads, whose historical points remained available.

boundedOmissions: One provisioned shard, one EFO consumer, one subscription, five tiny records; no resharding, throttling, failed writes, renewal, backlog larger than one EFO page, or network partition experiment.
Native absence means no datapoint in the precise queried dimension/time window after two bounded lags, not a universal AWS absence guarantee.
EFO replay was 118 seconds old but caught up in one event; it does not establish a positive behind-latest distribution. No EFO latency distribution inferred from admission or record-arrival timings.
Client close is not a server-delivery acknowledgment; final partial-minute service count exceeded client count by one.
CloudWatch ListMetrics discovery is eventually consistent; direct GetMetricStatistics evidence is retained independently.
Idle after client closure begins at the next full minute, avoiding the partial closing minute; idle after deregistration likewise begins at the next full minute.

currentCodeMismatches.measuredMismatch: streamMetricJobs/idleMetricSamples fabricate three Success zeros each idle minute; all six controlled complete idle minutes had missing Success series. The old dry_run fixture contains actual rejected requests and does not establish idle behavior.
currentCodeMismatches.minimalOwnershipChange: Remove the idle-only metric scheduler and its exclusively owned deadline/repository selection state and wiring; retain ordinary observed-request metric publication. Do not replace it with idle byte/age/consumer zeros.

currentCodeMismatches.measuredMismatch: Age samples use raw last arrival time only for nonempty results; native has a zero sample for both caught-up nonempty and empty successful reads.
currentCodeMismatches.minimalOwnershipChange: Have the successful GetRecords owner stage GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds from the page backlog/behind-latest observation on every success, with existing enhanced-name projection. Preserve request/record arrival timing distinctions; no new latency distribution.

currentCodeMismatches.measuredMismatch: Enhanced shard IncomingBytes is aggregated per batch, losing native per-record distribution (native 3 samples Min4 Max8 versus current 2 Min4 Max14). IncomingRecords batch aggregation matches and must remain.
currentCodeMismatches.minimalOwnershipChange: Keep stream IncomingBytes aggregation once per put operation. Stage enhanced shard IncomingBytes for each successfully appended record at the write owner; do not split shard IncomingRecords or add samples for failed records.

currentCodeMismatches.measuredMismatch: SubscribeToShard.RateExceeded is currently only emitted as 1 on rate/admission failures; successful native admission also emitted a 0 sample.
currentCodeMismatches.minimalOwnershipChange: Append consumer RateExceeded=0 alongside SubscribeToShard.Success=1 after successful lease admission. Keep error/admission metrics at the same request owner.

currentCodeMismatches.measuredMismatch: Current empty-event eligibility is one second; native complete empty minute emitted 12 events with 12 success/byte/record/behind-latest samples, approximately five-second heartbeats.
currentCodeMismatches.minimalOwnershipChange: Change the empty-heartbeat delivery owner rather than subsampling metrics: preserve metrics for each successful event, and align empty-heartbeat cadence with the measured five-second interval. Do not infer strict wall-clock scheduling or final-disconnect event counts from this run.

intentionallyUnchanged: Existing EFO consumer dimensions, enhanced outgoing dimensions, units, zero backlog values, and per-event metric production match the exercised observations.
No new EFO latency series: queried consumer latency names were absent in the bounded windows and are not listed in the cited Kinesis monitoring table.
No proof of a nonzero EFO MillisBehindLatest series; all delivered pages reached the tip.

No claim that the observed zero-valued dry-run Success datapoints were idle: dry_run.json sequences 63 and 94 include rejected requests. records.json was inspected and contains no CloudWatch calls (services were cloudtrail, iam, kinesis, sts); its EFO wire captures are not metric observations.
